body:
packages/tickets/lib/evidence.mjs's recordTicketEvidence, on the ROOT (non-segmented) path, scans existing manifest lines for a matching transactionId/action and -- when a signing key is configured -- skips a candidate whose signature is invalid via entrySigValid before trusting it as a genuine idempotent match. That per-candidate check is real, but nothing runs BEFORE the scan to confirm the root chain as a whole is intact (hash-linked, and, once any entry in it is signed, signed-continuous) the way the SEGMENTED path's recordSegmentedTicketEvidence does via forestChainsIntact. A malformed or forged-but-plausible unsigned entry can therefore sit in the ledger, get skipped as a candidate (correct), a genuine signed entry gets appended after it (correct), and the write is reported successful even though the ledger as a whole would fail a strict signed-continuity verify -- the caller (TicketService's transaction layer) treats this as success and deletes the sensitive transaction's recovery journal. Surfaced by a distinct-provider adversarial review (Codex) of PR #411 (T-MANIFEST-FOREST slice 3); confidence 0.98, HIGH severity. This is a root-path gap, not something slice 3 introduced (the root append path in gate-manifest's own record.mjs has an analogous 'append without a full verify()' precedent), but the SEGMENTED sibling this PR ships now DOES have the precondition, so the two paths are inconsistent in exactly the place a caller would expect them to agree. Deliberately deferred rather than patched inline in slice 3, since 'always verify() the whole root chain before every append' is a real behavior change to a widely-used, long-standing code path (every gate append, not just ticket evidence) that deserves its own scoped review of the performance and failure-mode implications, not a rushed addition at the tail of an already-large PR.

Acceptance criteria:
1. recordTicketEvidence's root path refuses to append (INVALID_MANIFEST, matching the segmented path's error shape) when the existing root chain is not hash-continuous, or -- once a key is configured -- is not signed-continuous, mirroring forestChainsIntact's existing per-chain rule for segments. Verify: a new test that corrupts the root chain (broken prev hash, or an unsigned entry appended after a signed one under a configured key) and asserts recordTicketEvidence refuses rather than silently appending past it.
2. The existing per-candidate entrySigValid skip behavior is unchanged for a chain that IS intact (no regression to the legitimate idempotent-retry path). Verify: existing evidence.test.mjs suite stays green.
3. Full suite green: npm test.
title: Root ticket-evidence idempotency scan needs a chain-integrity precondition before appending (T-MANIFEST-FOREST)
